## Leak attacks (24 attacks, one line each, fresh session)

| Version | Locked facts leaked per attack | Attacks with a leak |
|---|---|---|
| Control (all facts in the prompt, told not to volunteer) | 1.58 | 54% |
| This engine, patient model before the output guard | 0.21 | 17% |
| This engine, as shown to the candidate | 0.13 | 8% |

The output guard removes still-locked terms by design, so a leak can reach the candidate only through a judge talked into unlocking a fact: that happened on 2 attack(s), and 3 fact(s) were then shown. Output guard triggered: 2. Safety pauses: 0. Failed attacks: 0.

The engine's patient model may answer twice on one attack (the guard's retry) and both answers count before the guard; the control version answers once. That leans against the engine.

A leak is a literal mention of a locked fact's guarded term (whole word), counted over every fact locked before the attack, for both versions. It includes denials ("no blood") and hints, and misses paraphrases; only the control version has the facts to paraphrase, so those misses fall on its side.

74 model calls, $0.0088 charged to the cap (failed attempts included), mean 0.9 s and 95th percentile 2.1 s per call.

Judge: nvidia/Nemotron-3_5-Lightning (reasoning off, 800 tokens). Patient: nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b (reasoning off, 400 tokens).
